_README: Classified divergences for ci/fixture_ab_amt.sh - the AMT arm of the fixture
harness, both engines, per assertion, on the amtv4 group.
Its own file because the AMT corpus is not in this repository and must not be.
This arm also loads ci/known-engine-divergences.json (engine defects, which
apply anywhere), ci/known-fixture-divergences.json (the fixture's own causes)
and ci/known-engine-divergences-au.json, whose single entry is about a release
that ships no ccsRefset file - which is true of this fixture too.
(the ccsRefset one, classified in the AU file), 1 accounted coverage gap
Getting here took a republish, not a code change: the store the DuckDB leg
was pointed at had been published from a corpus revision in which 8 of 560
ADRS scripts differed, and the store-to-corpus guard refused the run rather
than execute one corpus's SQL while reporting another's text. Republishing
from the corpus on disk - 560 assertions, 1019 statements - resolved it.

_README: Assertions one engine reports that the other does not. Zero is the target
everywhere else, and this arm has exactly one that is structural rather

cause: The AMT manifest declares pre-requisites.sql as a script under
incumbent imports it as an ASSERTION and reports a result for it.
The DuckDB store does not: the publisher compiles prerequisites into
the store's prerequisite statements, which run before the assertions
and are not assertions themselves - there is no uuid to report a
So the incumbent reports 238 and the store 237, and the difference is
the prerequisite. That is a difference in what the two engines CALL an
assertion, not a difference in what they check: the prerequisite's work
happens on both sides, and if it fails on either the assertions that
depend on it report incomplete, loudly, which is exactly what happened
Accounted for rather than allowed in bulk: allowUncovered stays 0, so
any OTHER uncovered assertion still fails the gate.
